inputs.products: Millet-based chips and cookies made in Hyderabad. No maida, no palm oil. Sold on our website and Instagram. Launching a Snack Box sampler with 6 flavours.
inputs.instructions: Use Hinglish sparingly. Never mention competitors.

voice_summary: Warm, playful snack talk with a light desi flavour.
Keep Hinglish occasional and natural rather than making every line bilingual.
Make the six-flavour Snack Box sampler the hero of promotional posts.
Emphasise millet-based snacking, no maida and no palm oil without mentioning competitors.

tone.detail: Sound like a friendly host offering the audience something tasty to try, not a hard-selling advertiser.
Use light snack-time jokes, cheerful phrasing and compact punchlines suited to X.
Reference familiar Indian snacking moods and use sparing, accessible Hinglish rather than heavy slang.
Give posts a clear product focus and an easy next step, such as exploring the sampler on the website or Instagram.

target_audience.description: Health-conscious Indian snack buyers, likely digitally active urban consumers who want convenient alternatives to conventional chips and cookies and are open to discovering multiple flavours through a sampler.

content_themes.detail: Introduce the sampler as an easy way to explore six flavours without choosing just one.
Show that both savoury and sweet snack cravings can be met through the brand’s millet-based range.
Communicate these product attributes clearly and positively, without comparisons or competitor references.
Place the products in relatable moments such as chai breaks, desk snacking, evening cravings and sharing at home.
Use the brand’s Hyderabad origin as a point of local warmth and identity when relevant.
Write concise launch posts with a clear invitation to discover or order the Snack Box through the brand’s direct channels.

brand_hooks.hook: A Snack Box sampler containing six flavours
A range spanning millet-based chips and cookies
Products made without maida or palm oil
Available directly through the brand’s website and Instagram

style_rules.language: Primarily English with occasional, sparing Hinglish
style_rules.sentence_style: Short, conversational sentences with one clear product point, a light playful turn and a direct call to action.
signature_patterns: Relatable snack-time setup followed by a playful product reveal
Brief Hinglish interjection used as the punchline rather than throughout the post
Six-flavour choice or variety framed as a happy dilemma
Product benefit followed by a simple discovery or purchase prompt

dos: Lead with appetite, variety or a relatable snacking moment before adding product details.
Make the six-flavour Snack Box the central hook during the launch campaign.
State “no maida” and “no palm oil” accurately and without turning them into medical claims.
Use simple, widely understood Hinglish only occasionally.
Include a concise call to action directing people to the website or Instagram when appropriate.
donts: Do not mention, tag or allude to competitors.
Do not imply that the snacks treat health conditions or guarantee health outcomes.
Do not overload posts with Hindi, regional slang, emojis or hashtags.
Do not invent flavour names, prices, discounts, nutrition claims or availability details.
Do not sound preachy, clinical or guilt-driven about snacking.
assumptions: The target audience is inferred because no customer demographics were provided.
Everyday occasions such as chai breaks, work breaks and evening cravings are suggested creative contexts, not confirmed use cases.
Light emoji and hashtag use are defaults because no posts or research were available to establish an existing pattern.
The sentence style and signature patterns are recommended for X rather than derived from existing brand posts.
No flavour names, prices, offers, shipping details or launch date were provided, so posts should not add them.
The suggested avoidance of medical, weight-loss and superiority language is a strategic safeguard, not an explicit user instruction.

tweets.text: Six flavours. One Snack Box. No need to choose just one. Meet the millet-based sampler made for curious snackers—and happy dilemmas. Explore it on our website.
tweets.why: Leads with the six-flavour Snack Box and its easy discovery benefit.

tweets.text: Chai break choice: millet-based chips for the crunch or millet-based cookies for the sweet finish? Pick your side 👇
tweets.why: Uses a relatable chai-time this-or-that with the chips-and-cookies range.

tweets.angle: meme or parody format that fits the voice: a fake equation, 'POV:', a fake notice or announcement, 'nobody: / me:', a chapter title. Don't default to 'POV: you opened [app]'
tweets.text: Official snack equation: millet + crunch − maida − palm oil = dibba mysteriously empty again.
tweets.why: Turns the no-maida, no-palm-oil attributes into a playful fake equation.

tweets.text: Desk-snack tip: portion your snack before the first email spiral begins. Keep chips for the crunchy mood and cookies for the chai mood—future you will appreciate the planning.
tweets.why: Offers a practical portioning tip for everyday desk and chai breaks.

tweets.text: Made in Hyderabad, ready for your evening chai scene. Bring home the six-flavour Snack Box and let everyone find their favourite. Find us on Instagram.
tweets.why: Connects Hyderabad roots with a warm, shareable chai-time occasion.

tweets.text: Fill in the blank: My Snack Box flavour ranking would cause family drama because ________. Six flavours are ready to be judged—discover the sampler on our website or Instagram.
tweets.why: Uses a reply-friendly prompt while spotlighting the six-flavour sampler.

tweets.angle: wordplay on the product or category
tweets.text: Choosing one flavour? That’s a snackrilege. The Snack Box brings six to the table, so your taste buds can hold a proper meeting.
tweets.why: Uses category wordplay to frame six-flavour discovery as a happy dilemma.

tweets.text: How to share a Snack Box: 1. Put all six flavours out. 2. Pass the millet-based chips and cookies around. 3. Trade until everyone finds a favourite. Simple, na?
tweets.why: Gives a quick how-to for choosing between savoury and sweet millet snacks.
tweets.revisionReason: Repeats tweet two’s chips-versus-cookies choice too closely.
tweets.originalText: How to handle two snack moods: 1. Pick millet-based chips when you want crunch. 2. Pick millet-based cookies when chai needs company. 3. Keep both nearby. Simple, na?

tweets.angle: what makes it different (only from the brief)
tweets.text: Crunchy chips, chai-ready cookies, six flavours to explore. All millet-based, with no maida and no palm oil. Meet the Snack Box on our website.
tweets.why: Clearly presents the product attributes and sampler as the point of difference.
tweets.revisionReason: Accurate but list-like and forgettable for a promotional post.
tweets.originalText: Millet-based chips and cookies. No maida. No palm oil. Six flavours packed into one easy sampler. Pick your Snack Box on our website.

tweets.angle: easy first step to try or buy
tweets.text: Start with one box for chai breaks, desk cravings and passing around at home. The six-flavour Snack Box makes trying the range easy—order through Instagram.
tweets.why: Positions the sampler as an easy first purchase for familiar snack moments.
